predecessors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
predecessors.text: the Rajasthan feudatory lands: the Chahamanas 'served the Gurjara-Pratiharas as vassals' and 'Vakpatiraja I made an attempt to overthrow the Gurjara-Pratihara suzerainty'; Simharaja 'asserted…

successors.name: Ghurid dynasty
successors.text: Ajmer and the Chahamana kingdom, which 'Muhammad of Ghor appointed Prithviraja's son Govindaraja IV as a vassal' to hold in 1192; Hariraja was defeated by the Ghurids in 1194

successors.name: Chahamanas of Ranastambhapura
successors.text: Ranthambore: 'Govindaraja was granted the fief of Ranthambore by the Ghurids' and 'established a new branch of the dynasty'

ledger.x: c. 944: Simharaja makes the Chahamanas independent at Shakambhari. 'Simharaja assumed the title Maharajadhiraja' and 'asserted independence' of the Gurjara-Pratiharas; Vakpatiraja I had 'made an attempt to overthrow the Gurjara-Pratihara suzerainty' in the 10th…

c. 1040: Bhoja takes Shakambhari. 'During the reign of Viryarama (r. c. 1040 CE), the Paramara king Bhoja invaded the Chahamana kingdom' and 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period'; the Bhoja page: he 'defeated and killed Viryarama'.
1056 (bridge): the northern and western margins leave the Chahamana shape.
c. 1110: Ajayaraja II moves the capital to Ajmer. 'Ajayaraja II moved the capital there in the early 12th century' (Ajayameru, modern Ajmer); his reign begins in 1110 on the table.

c. 1151: Vigraharaja IV takes Delhi and Hansi from the Tomaras. 'greatly expanded the Chahamana territories, and captured Delhi from the Tomaras'; the quoted reference: 'In 1151 the Tomar Rajput rulers (and original builders) of Delhi were overthrown by Visal Dev'; the Tomara page: 'had captured Dhillika (Delhi) and…
1183: the Mahoba campaign ends without annexation (R.
1192: the Second Battle of Tarain ends the contest in a Ghurid victory.
1192: Delhi and Haryana to the Ghurids.
1194: Hariraja is defeated by the Ghurids and the Chahamana dynasty of Shakambhari ends.

wars.name: Ghaznavid raids on the Chahamanas
wars.outcome: 'The subsequent Chahamana kings faced several Ghaznavid raids' (no year); 'Ajayaraja II (r. c.

wars.name: Bhoja's invasion of Shakambhari
wars.outcome: Bhoja invaded in the reign of Viryarama, 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period' and killed Viryarama; Chamundaraja restored the Chahamanas.

wars.name: Chahamana-Tomara wars
wars.outcome: Arnoraja 'raided the Tomara territory'; Vigraharaja IV captured Delhi and Hansi c.

wars.name: Prithviraj III-Chandela war (Mahoba)
wars.outcome: Mahoba sacked in 1182-83; no annexation (Talbot), or a short-lived one (R.

wars.name: Chahamana-Chaulukya war of Prithviraja III
wars.outcome: Prithviraj 'invaded Gujarat but could not gain much success and concluded a peace treaty with Chaulukya Bhima II' (before 1187).

wars.name: First Battle of Tarain
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor captured Tabarhindah (Bathinda) in 1190-1191; Prithviraj's army 'decisively defeated the Ghurids' at Tarain in 1191.

wars.name: Second Battle of Tarain
wars.outcome: Decisive Ghurid victory near Tarain; Prithviraj killed or executed; Govindaraja IV installed at Ajmer as a Ghurid vassal.

wars.name: Ghurid conquest of Hariraja
wars.outcome: Hariraja dethroned Govindaraja IV in 1192 and was defeated by Qutb al-Din Aibak, 'in 1194 CE'; the dynasty of Shakambhari ended.
